zones.name: The net
zones.text: The net crosses the full 10 m width. It is 88 cm high in the middle and 92 cm at the posts, a little lower than a tennis net, so volleys and net play matter a lot.

zones.name: Service line
zones.text: Each side has a service line 6.95 m from the net. The server stands behind it, and the serve must land in the service box diagonally opposite.

zones.name: Centre line
zones.text: The centre line splits each service area into a left box and a right box. Serves always cross diagonally, like in tennis.

zones.name: Back wall
zones.text: The back wall is glass, usually 3 m tall with metal mesh above it to about 4 m. After the ball bounces on the ground, it can hit this wall and you can still play it.

zones.name: Side walls
zones.text: Side walls are glass near the back and metal mesh towards the net. Glass gives a clean rebound; mesh can make the ball bounce in odd ways.

zones.name: Service box
zones.text: The serve must bounce inside this box. It may then hit the glass, but if it hits the mesh after bouncing it is a fault.

zones.name: Playing area
zones.text: The whole court is 20 m long and 10 m wide, so each side is a 10 x 10 m square. That's about a third of a tennis court.

shots.name: Volley
shots.text: Hitting the ball before it bounces, usually near the net. Short, firm punches beat big swings.
shots.tip: Keep the racket up in front of your chest.

shots.name: Lob (globo)
shots.text: A high, deep ball over the net players. It's the shot that wins back the net when you're defending.
shots.tip: Aim deep, close to the back glass, so it's hard to smash.

shots.name: Contrapared
shots.text: Hitting the ball into your own back wall so it rebounds over the net. A rescue shot when a lob has gone past you.
shots.tip: Hit up and into the glass; let the wall do the work.

shots.name: Bandeja
shots.text: A controlled overhead with slice, played when the opponents lob you. It isn't meant to win the point. It keeps you at the net.
shots.tip: Think 'placement, not power'. Stay at the net afterwards.

shots.name: Chiquita
shots.text: A soft, low ball from the back of the court that drops at the feet of the net players. It's a transition shot that lets your team move forward.
shots.tip: Don't try it from deep in the court; you need control.

shots.name: Víbora
shots.text: An attacking overhead with sidespin and more pace than the bandeja. The name means 'viper', because it skids away at an awkward angle.

shots.name: Rulo
shots.text: A topspin smash aimed across the court towards the side fence, where the ball takes an unpredictable bounce. A lower-risk way to attack a short lob.
shots.tip: Aim cross-court at the mesh, not the glass.

shots.name: Bajada
shots.text: An attacking shot taken high after the ball comes off the back wall. It turns a defensive ball into an attack.
shots.tip: Let the ball come off the glass and meet it on the way down.

shots.name: Smash (remate)
shots.text: The full-power overhead. It can bounce out of the court to win the point, but a weak smash gives the ball back.
shots.tip: Only smash the short, high lobs.

shots.name: Dejada (drop shot)
shots.text: A soft shot with backspin that dies just over the net. Best when the opponents are stuck at the back.
shots.tip: Disguise it like a normal volley.

glossary: Social format where you change partner every round and keep the points you win.
Attacking shot taken after the ball rebounds high off the back wall.
Controlled sliced overhead that keeps your team at the net.
Soft, low ball aimed at the net players' feet.
Hitting the ball into your own back wall so it goes over the net.
The glass walls at the back and sides of the court.
A flat, fast overhead between a bajada and a víbora, often called the knife.
Drop shot that lands just over the net with backspin.
The player on the right side of the court (deuce side).
Lob: a high, deep ball over the net players.
At 40-40, one deciding point wins the game. The receiving pair chooses the side.
Zig-zag shoe sole that grips on sandy artificial grass courts.
A serve that touches the net and then lands in the right box is replayed. Also used when a point is replayed after an interruption.
The metal mesh fence around the court.
Like an Americano, but each new round is made from the leaderboard so similar scores meet.
Thin, soft tape wrapped over the handle for grip and to absorb sweat.
Wall. Any shot played off the glass.
Smash hit hard enough to bounce out over the back wall.
The player on the left side of the court, often the more attacking player.
Format where fixed pairs each play every other pair once.
Topspin smash aimed cross-court at the side fence.
Playing the ball after it has come off the wall.
Running out through the door to play a ball that has left the court. Only allowed where the club or event permits it.
The serve. It is hit underarm, after one bounce, at or below waist height.
A newer deuce format in the 2026 rules where play goes through advantages before a final deciding point.
Volley: hitting the ball before it bounces.
Attacking overhead with sidespin; 'viper' in Spanish.
Hitting the ball backwards between your legs.
